Jackson’s Reel

Maeve Flanagan playing this reel on the fiddle: http://comhaltas.ie/music/detail/comhaltaslive_256_3_a_fiddle_solo_from_maeve_flanagan/

Her uncle Brian Conway is among the past pupils of the late Andy McGann, who directly learned music from Michael Coleman. Coleman is believed to have popularised this reel.

↳ Posted by slainte on April 11th, 2013.

Jackson`s Reel

I came across 3 different reels called Jackson`s Reel on Youtube. The main tune is probably John and James Kelly`s version but the othes are nice too. Seems to be a feature of Irish trad tunes to have several names, a bit like the Clare jig or Mug of Brown Ale, Hand me down the Tackle or Pure Drop, The Belfast hornpipe or the Sweeps hornpipe, the Derry Air or Danny Boy, The New Mown Meadows or Joe Mhaire Mhicilin and we also have that phenomenon where several different tunes are lumped under the one title as above and another example is the Copperplate. No wonder it`s a confusing business!
